title: Code and derived results for: Paths or completion? Testing t-norm composition in a graded health knowledge graph of depressive symptoms
description: Analysis pipeline and derived results (relation matrices, edge lists, null-model, bootstrap and t-norm inference results, clinical review form) for a fuzzy relation graph of nine PHQ-9 symptoms and 15 correlates built from NHANES 2007–2018. NHANES source files are public and are downloaded by download_nhanes.py; checksums of the files used are in raw/MANIFEST.md5. Versions 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 add predictors without paths, parametric t-norms, scale transformations, withheld relation blocks with cross-validated completion rank, simulations matched to the data's noise and scale, a strength-preserving null and the literature-search records; and, in 1.2.0, RQ3 with the periods swapped, on PSU-split halves of 2013–2018, with binary PHQ-9 items and under every sensitivity setting. Version 1.3.0 adds regularised and logit soft-impute, NMF, prevalence-and-block regression, Katz, common-neighbour, Adamic–Adar, resource-allocation and personalised-PageRank indices, a learned path model, within-block and per-source evaluation (NDCG@5), concept-jackknife intervals, calibration fitted on measured pairs in the withheld design, random masking and cold start, age–sex standardised and signed relations, and a respondent-level simulation of chained versus latent-factor generation. Version 1.4.0 adds the prevalence-odds identity by pair type, block-wise rank-1 completion, non-linear PHQ-9 item mappings, shrinkage and exclusion of low-information pairs, jackknife repeated replication intervals, a clustered simulation of interval coverage, a withheld-block summary with sign tests, an exact O(n^3) leave-dyad-out composition algorithm (fast_compose.py) and a network figure. The clinical review of membership functions was carried out by Van An Phan Thi, co-author from version 1.8.1. Version 1.5.0 adds audit_extensions.py (forward-only masking check, rank selection by cross-validation, DistMult and ComplEx baselines, strong-tail metrics, a clinical query, alternative association measures including graphical-lasso partial correlations, and further sensitivity analyses) and a 100-replicate coverage run; revision7.py is renamed sensitivity_and_inference.py. Version 1.6.0 adds generalization_checks.py: evaluation on the symmetric relation (276 dyads) in the temporal, split-half and swapped designs with JRR intervals and a prevalence-partialled Spearman correlation on the directed relation; JRR intervals and Holm-adjusted p-values for every predictor against the product, precision at K = 20 and 50, rho on positive target relations and the development relation as its own target; JRR intervals for the alternative association measures; development graphs thinned to their strongest edges, with best-path lengths and path counts; random withholding of 10–75% of dyads; cold start with 1, 3 or 6 anchor relations per concept; JRR intervals for the withheld relation types per block and pair-weighted, with ranks 1–5; replicate counts, tie handling, the direct-edge ceiling and effective sample sizes for the clinical query; graphs by age group and sex; never-married respondents scored 0 or 1; and split halves within 2015–2018. figures8.py draws the missingness summary figure, and the network figure (figures7.py) uses marker shapes and dashed between-community edges for grayscale printing. Version 1.7.0 adds mechanism_checks.py (composition of the symmetric relation re-directed by prevalence odds; JRR with ranks re-chosen in every replicate and NMF and ComplEx in the Holm family; the clinical query in the 20 split halves; random and source-based thinning with zero-prediction shares and AUC; soft-impute on both scales in every design; minimum, ComplEx and re-chosen ranks for withheld relation types; a respondent-level simulation with cut or continuous measurement and whole types withheld), scale_simulation.py (simulated graphs of 48 and 96 concepts), and confirmatory/ (a plan registered before the NHANES 2005-2006 files were downloaded, run_2005.py and its results). The figure script figures8.py draws four panels. Version 1.8.0 adds rigor_checks.py: the exact empirical decomposition of edge direction and the size of its prevalence-odds approximation (path-cancellation error, relative error, agreement of directed and re-directed best paths); completion rank and soft-impute penalty re-chosen inside every single-dyad mask; the illustrative query per symptom with split-half hit rates; run times of every step; post-registration two one-sided equivalence tests with margins 0.03 and 0.05; and counts of clipped and positive relations by period. figures8.py adds uncertainty bars. Version 1.8.1 changes metadata only: Van An Phan Thi is listed as co-author, matching the revised manuscript; code and results are those of version 1.8.0. Version 1.9.0 adds review3_checks.py: the probability that each registered decision rule is met under true differences of 0, 0.03 and 0.05; soft-impute on the raw scale, the logit scale and the scale chosen by cross-validation on the other blocks when whole relation types are withheld, with JRR intervals in the cross-period and the registered 2005-2006 designs; t-norm outputs mapped monotonically onto the scale of the symmetric relation before re-direction; soft-impute with the penalty grid extended to 5; diagnostics for soft-impute with one anchor relation; and standard deviations for random thinning with soft-impute on both scales. figures8.py plots soft-impute on the logit scale in every panel. The registered decisions are unchanged.
